Subject: Vertex Health — hosting path recommendation and initial GPU tiling thoughts

Hi Ana,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Per our discussion, I pulled together a short recommendation for the hosting posture (Private deployment vs Dedicated reserved capacity) tied to your regulatory and uptime needs. Big picture: we can reliably meet Vertex Health's SLOs with either option, but the economic and procurement implications differ across the pilot and scale phases.

Quick summary (details attached):
- Pilot (Q3): recommend Dedicated reserved pool (medium tile) for faster onboarding and predictable throughput; Redwood can provision burstable headroom for the initial 2–3 month pilot.
- Production/regulated (post-pilot): evaluate Private deployment if you require customer-managed networking and on-prem integrations; otherwise, a larger Dedicated fleet with isolated tenant pools gives similar isolation guarantees with simpler procurement.

Ask: can you confirm whether your security team will require an on-premable audit trail (HSM/KMS integration) for the pilot, or is that only a hard requirement for production? That will shift the recommended procurement path.

I've attached a short GPU tiling proposal and a perf benchmark snapshot to help the procurement team with sizing estimates. If useful, we can run a focused cost/latency tradeoff test on a representative workload next week.

Next steps I propose:
1) You + procurement confirm the KMS/HSM requirement and any formal audit gating.
2) Redwood sends a two-option procurement packet (Dedicated mid-commit and Private appliance baseline) including pricing, initial MPA redlines, and provisioning timelines.
3) Quick 30-minute alignment session with Dev/Infra (we can include Dev Patel and Laura).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the attachment.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Jordan / Dev —

Looping in Marissa for commercial angle. Quick internal take for the procurement asks Ana raised:

1) Timeline to convert Dedicated -> Private (high level):
- Assessment + network prep: 1–2 weeks (customer-owned network configs, firewall rules).
- Private control plane install + KMS/HSM integration: 2–3 weeks (depends on HSM vendor cadence).
- Data migration + validation: 1 week for config/metadata; model re-pull can be parallelized if permissions/entitlements are ready.
Total (best-case): ~4–6 weeks. Add 1–2 weeks for on-prem hardware lead time if they want on-prem GPUs instead of cloud-hosted Private.

2) NRE (non-recurring engineering) and one-time costs (ballpark):
- Private control plane delivery & KMS hookup: $45k–$90k depending on HSM complexity.
- On-prem hardware procurement: variable — we usually show OPEX alternative via Dedicated reserved capacity to avoid large upfront spend.
- Data egress / migration engineering: $8k–$15k typical for a pilot-sized dataset.

3) SLA / credit implications:
- Dedicated: SLA sits with Redwood hosted infra; credits per contract SLOs.
- Private: SLA is customer-managed for infra; Redwood SLA limited to control plane and support obligations. The contractual fallback (Dedicated -> Private) will require explicit rollback and acceptance windows; we should surface possible service availability windows during migration and a contingency plan (dual-write or read-only cutover).

4) Sizing note: Vertex pilot workload profile shows spiky inference (bursty daytime calls) with long-ish contexts (2–4k tokens) for triage flow. For pilot we recommend staging a 4-GPU tile (A100x) per shard to keep tail latency < 250ms p95 and allow 2x concurrency. For production (50k RPS-equivalent daily), plan for a tiled fleet of 24–32 GPUs with KV cache warmers and prefix caching to control costs.

I've attached a short capex vs opex slide to the draft packet — Jordan, can you fold this into the MPA package and include a clear conversion-runway clause? Marissa, thoughts on discounting if they commit to a 12-month reserved pool vs buying Private?

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference

Ana / Procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Per Laura and Dev's notes above, here is a succinct set of options we can present to procurement next Wednesday. I attached an MPA draft with redlines and a short spreadsheet estimating tile counts and cost bands.

Option A — Pilot-first, Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended for speed):
- Timeline: Provisioned in ~7–10 business days.
- Sizing: 4-GPU tile (A100-class) for pilot, warm KV caches; scales to 24 GPUs if pilot targets met.
- Pros: Fast onboarding, lower initial NRE, predictable monthly OPEX.
- Cons: Conversion to Private later incurs NRE (~$45k–$90k) and migration window (4–6 weeks).
- SLA: Redwood hosted SLA applies. Credits explicitly stated in clause 7; we propose a 99.9% monthly uptime SLO with step-down credits.

Option B — Baseline Private (for compliance-first customers):
- Timeline: ~4–8 weeks (depends on HSM/hardware lead time).
- Sizing: Appliance control plane + 8–16 GPUs for baseline (smaller than dedicated ramp but higher upfront cost).
- Pros: Customer-managed networking, stronger isolation controls, full KMS/HSM model.
- Cons: Higher NRE and potential capital expenditure; longer time to value.

Commercial asks we propose to include in the procurement packet:
- A conversion runway clause: if Vertex commits to a 12-month reserved pool and later needs Private, Redwood will cap the NRE to $55k (midpoint) and provide a 30% credit on unused reserved months applied to installation costs.
- A pilot credit: 10% off first 2 months of Dedicated usage if Vertex signs the pilot MPA within 10 business days of this email.

Attachments: MPA_draft_redlines.pdf; Vertex_GPU_Tiling_Proposal_v1.xlsx; perf_benchmarks_q2.csv

If that looks good, I'll send the formal procurement packet (MPA + pricing spreadsheet + timelines) by EOD Monday so Ana can loop Procurement. Happy to join the procurement call next Wednesday.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
